steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our FedTracker paper on copyright protection of federated learning models. Explain the model leakage problem, why existing DNN and FL watermarking only covers ownership verification and not traceability, how our framework handles both, the challenges we solve, and close with contributions and a roadmap of the paper.

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. FL and model leakage
- FL: popular framework for distributed training of DL models without sharing private messages
- applied in privacy-sensitive domains: object detection, medical image analysis, recommendation systems
- meets privacy needs, produces high-quality models
- collaborative training -> model available to many participants -> model leakage

2. Copyright concerns
- model leakage: individual Client maliciously distributes / sells FL model for personal gain = model leaker
- infringes copyright of whole FL group (innocent Clients, Servers); detecting infringement, protecting IP critical
- ownership verification: verify ownership when model illegally distributed; charge unauthorized user outside group with tort; model is IP of FL group, not any individual; legal use needs group consent
- traceability: disclose identity of culprit among participants who leaked to third parties; new requirement, not addressed before

3. DNN watermarks
- proposed to protect DNN copyright: parameter-based and backdoor-based
- parameter-based: embed into parameters or their distribution; multi-bit info; extraction needs white-box access -> limits application
- backdoor-based: use backdoor attack to insert triggers; black-box verification; usually zero-bit (presence/absence, not identity bit string)

4. Watermarks in FL
- WAFFLE: first FL watermarking scheme; Server embeds backdoor watermark; retraining step after aggregation
- Liu et al. and Li et al.: Clients embed parameter-based and backdoor-based watermarks into global model
- all only ownership verification; no traceability of model leakers; group can prove ownership but cannot find leakers among them

5. FedTracker
- goal: FL copyright protection with ownership verification + traceability; FedTracker first to offer both; Fig. 1
- bi-level scheme: global watermark embedded in aggregated global model each iteration -> extract and verify ownership on infringement; server inserts unique local fingerprint per Client before distribution -> trace leaker
- challenge 1: utility with lack of natural data; server has no training data -> out-of-distribution trigger set -> may compromise utility
- challenge 2: discrimination of different models; many fingerprints -> higher requirement on identifiability and robustness
- solution 1: Continual Learning (CL) based watermark embedding; FL task and watermark task as different domains; utility drop = catastrophic forgetting; inspired by Gradient Episodic Memory (GEM); Section IV-B
- solution 2: fingerprint generation minimizing maximal distance between fingerprints; Fingerprint Similarity Score (FSS), continuous vs discrete hamming distance -> finer-grained; watermark and fingerprints in different parts of model; Section IV-C

## Contributions
- FedTracker: first FL ownership verification and traceability framework; bi-level scheme (global watermark, local fingerprint); fidelity and robustness against various attacks
- CL-based watermark embedding for FL; keeps utility on primitive and watermark task
- optimization-based fingerprint generation + FSS metric -> distinguish fingerprints, trace culprit

## Roadmap
- Section II background; Section III problem formulation (ownership verification, traceability, threat model); Section IV FedTracker procedure and solutions; Section V implementation; Section VI experiments; Section VII conclusion

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Federated Learning (FL) has become one of the most popular frameworks for training Deep Learning (DL) models in a distributed way without sharing private messages. Today FL is widely used in many privacy-sensitive domains, like object detection, medical image analysis, recommendation systems and so on. FL meets the privacy needs of the data owners and still produces high-quality models for the community. But because training in FL is collaborative, the model is available to multiple participants, and this can lead to the model leakage issue in FL.

Model leakage in FL means that an individual Client maliciously distributes or sells the FL model without authorization for personal gain. We call these malicious Clients the model leakers. This misbehavior infringes the legitimate copyright of the whole FL group, which includes innocent Clients and Servers. So detecting copyright infringement and protecting intellectual property rights has become a critical issue in FL. FL copyright protection has two major concerns, ownership verification and traceability. Ownership verification means verifying the ownership of the FL model when it is illegally distributed and charging the unauthorized user outside the FL group with tort. The FL model should be seen as the intellectual property of the FL group and not of any individual, and any legal use of the FL model should have the consent of the FL group. Traceability means disclosing the identity of the culprit among the FL participants who illegally distributes the model to third parties outside the FL group. This is a new requirement for protecting the copyright of the FL model, and to our best knowledge it has not been addressed before.

DNN watermarks have been proposed to protect the copyright of Deep Neural Networks (DNN), and there are parameter-based watermarks and backdoor-based watermarks. Parameter-based watermark methods embed personal watermarks into the parameters of the DNN models or into the distribution of the parameters. They can give multi-bit information for verification, but to extract parameter-based watermarks you need white-box access to the model, which limits where they can be applied. Backdoor-based watermark methods on the other hand use backdoor attack to insert specific triggers that identify the ownership of the model. Backdoor-based watermarks can be verified with black-box access, but they are usually zero-bit. This means the watermark can only show whether the watermark is present or absent, and not a bit string that represents identity.

Some recent works also try applying DNN watermarks to FL copyright protection. WAFFLE is the first watermarking scheme designed for FL, and in it the Server embeds the backdoor-based watermarks into the FL model. WAFFLE does a retraining step after federated aggregation to embed the watermark. Liu et al. and Li et al. let the Clients embed both parameter-based and backdoor-based watermarks into the global model. However, the existing works only focus on ownership verification. None of them gives traceability of the model leakers for FL models. So even if the FL group can prove that it owns the FL model when infringement happens, it cannot detect the model leakers that are hidden among its members.

5. FedTracker

- bi-level scheme: global watermark embedded in aggregated global model each iteration -> extract and verify ownership on infringement; server inserts unique local fingerprint per Client before distribution -> trace leaker
- challenge 1: utility with lack of natural data; server has no training data -> out-of-distribution trigger set -> may compromise utility
- challenge 2: discrimination of different models; many fingerprints -> higher requirement on identifiability and robustness
- solution 1: Continual Learning (CL) based watermark embedding; FL task and watermark task as different domains; utility drop = catastrophic forgetting; inspired by Gradient Episodic Memory (GEM); Section IV-B
- solution 2: fingerprint generation minimizing maximal distance between fingerprints; Fingerprint Similarity Score (FSS), continuous vs discrete hamming distance -> finer-grained; watermark and fingerprints in different parts of model; Section IV-C

- CL-based watermark embedding for FL; keeps utility on primitive and watermark task
- optimization-based fingerprint generation + FSS metric -> distinguish fingerprints, trace culprit

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Federated Learning (FL) has become one of the most popular frameworks for training Deep Learning (DL) models in a distributed way without sharing private messages. Today FL is widely used in many privacy-sensitive domains, like object detection, medical image analysis, recommendation systems and so on. FL meets the privacy needs of the data owners and still produces high-quality models for the community. But because training in FL is collaborative, the model is available to multiple participants, and this can lead to the model leakage issue in FL.

Model leakage in FL means that an individual Client maliciously distributes or sells the FL model without authorization for personal gain. We call these malicious Clients the model leakers. This misbehavior infringes the legitimate copyright of the whole FL group, which includes innocent Clients and Servers. So detecting copyright infringement and protecting intellectual property rights has become a critical issue in FL. FL copyright protection has two major concerns, ownership verification and traceability. Ownership verification means verifying the ownership of the FL model when it is illegally distributed and charging the unauthorized user outside the FL group with tort. The FL model should be seen as the intellectual property of the FL group and not of any individual, and any legal use of the FL model should have the consent of the FL group. Traceability means disclosing the identity of the culprit among the FL participants who illegally distributes the model to third parties outside the FL group. This is a new requirement for protecting the copyright of the FL model, and to our best knowledge it has not been addressed before.

DNN watermarks have been proposed to protect the copyright of Deep Neural Networks (DNN), and there are parameter-based watermarks and backdoor-based watermarks. Parameter-based watermark methods embed personal watermarks into the parameters of the DNN models or into the distribution of the parameters. They can give multi-bit information for verification, but to extract parameter-based watermarks you need white-box access to the model, which limits where they can be applied. Backdoor-based watermark methods on the other hand use backdoor attack to insert specific triggers that identify the ownership of the model. Backdoor-based watermarks can be verified with black-box access, but they are usually zero-bit. This means the watermark can only show whether the watermark is present or absent, and not a bit string that represents identity.

Some recent works also try applying DNN watermarks to FL copyright protection. WAFFLE is the first watermarking scheme designed for FL, and in it the Server embeds the backdoor-based watermarks into the FL model. WAFFLE does a retraining step after federated aggregation to embed the watermark. Liu et al. and Li et al. let the Clients embed both parameter-based and backdoor-based watermarks into the global model. However, the existing works only focus on ownership verification. None of them gives traceability of the model leakers for FL models. So even if the FL group can prove that it owns the FL model when infringement happens, it cannot detect the model leakers that are hidden among its members.

We want to design an FL copyright protection framework that gives both ownership verification and traceability for the FL model. In this paper we present FedTracker, which is the first FL model protection framework that offers both. Fig. 1 illustrates the problem and our framework. We design a bi-level protection scheme, where one level is for ownership verification and the other is for traceability. On the first level, FedTracker embeds a global watermark into the aggregated global model in each iteration. When copyright infringement happens, the FL group can extract the watermark and verify ownership. On the second level, before the model is distributed in each iteration, the server inserts a unique local fingerprint for each Client so that each model can be identified. The model leaker can then be traced by disclosing the identification inside the model.

But there are two main challenges in implementing this kind of framework:

- It is hard to keep the utility of the model when natural data is lacking. The server is assumed to have no access to the training data, so it has to embed a watermark trigger set that is out of the distribution of natural data. This may hurt the utility of the model a lot.

- It is hard to guarantee that different models can be told apart. We have to embed and compare many different fingerprints from different Clients, so the identifiability and robustness of the Clients' fingerprints need to be higher.

To tackle these challenges, first we propose a watermark embedding algorithm based on Continual Learning (CL) that improves the utility of the watermarked model. We treat the primitive task of FL and the watermark embedding task as learning data from different domains. The drop in utility can be attributed to catastrophic forgetting when a different task is learned. Inspired by the Gradient Episodic Memory (GEM), we design a CL-based embedding algorithm for the FL scenario, and so the utility is better preserved while the watermark is embedded. Our CL-based watermark embedding algorithm is introduced in Section IV-B.

Second, to better differentiate the models of different Clients, we generate the fingerprints by minimizing the maximal distance between fingerprints. We also propose a Fingerprint Similarity Score (FSS) that measures the similarity between the extracted fingerprint and the Clients' fingerprints. Traditional hamming distance has a discrete output, but the output of FSS is continuous, so FSS gives a more fine-grained measurement and can discriminate different fingerprints better. We also embed the watermark and the fingerprints into different parts of the model, which lowers their mutual impact and makes both mechanisms more effective. The details are in Section IV-C.

## I-A Contributions

Our main contributions are:

- We propose FedTracker, the first FL ownership verification and traceability framework. In FedTracker, the bi-level protection scheme, with the global watermark mechanism and the local fingerprint mechanism, gives ownership verification and traceability respectively. Experiments show FedTracker also gives tremendous fidelity and robustness against various attacks.

- Inspired by Continual Learning (CL), we design a CL-based watermark embedding algorithm for the FL scenario. It keeps the utility of the FL model on both the primitive task and the watermark task while the watermark is embedded.

- We propose a fingerprint generation method based on optimization and a new metric called Fingerprint Similarity Score (FSS). These two help to distinguish different fingerprints better and make tracing the culprit more effective.

## I-B Roadmap

The rest of the paper is organized like this. Section II introduces the background knowledge of FedTracker. Section III formulates the copyright protection problem in FL, including the definitions of ownership verification and traceability and the threat model. Section IV gives the procedure of FedTracker and the solutions to the key challenges above. Section V describes the implementation of FedTracker in detail. Section VI presents the experiments that evaluate FedTracker's performance, and Section VII concludes the paper.

steps.text:
Federated Learning (FL) [1] has become one of the most popular frameworks for distributedly training Deep Learning (DL) models without sharing private messages. FL is nowadays widely applied in various privacy-sensitive domains, such as object detection [2,3], medical image analysis [4,5,6], recommendation systems [7,8] and so on. FL meets the privacy needs of the data owners while producing high-quality models for the community. However, collaborative training in FL makes the model available to multiple participants, which may lead to the model leakage issue in FL.

Model leakage in FL refers to the malicious distribution or unauthorized sale of FL models by an individual Client for personal gain. These malicious Clients are called model leakers. Such misbehavior infringes the legitimate copyright of the entire FL group, including innocent Clients and Servers. Detecting copyright infringement and protecting intellectual property rights has therefore become a critical issue in FL. There are two major concerns in FL copyright protection: ownership verification and traceability. Ownership verification involves verifying the ownership of the FL model when it is illegally distributed and charging the unauthorized user outside the FL group with tort. The FL model should be considered the intellectual property of the FL group instead of any individual, and any legal use of the FL model should be made with the consent of the FL group. Traceability refers to disclosing the identity of the culprit among the FL participants who illegally distributes the model to third parties outside the FL group. It is a new requirement for protecting the copyright of the FL model, which to our best knowledge has not been addressed before.

To protect the copyright of Deep Neural Networks (DNN), DNN watermarks [9,10], including parameter-based and backdoor-based watermarks, have been proposed. Parameter-based watermark methods embed personal watermarks into the parameters or the distribution of the parameters of DNN models [11,12,13,14]. They can provide multi-bit information for verification, but extracting parameter-based watermarks needs white-box access to the model, which limits their application. In contrast, backdoor-based watermark methods [15,16,17,18] take advantage of backdoor attack [19] to insert specific triggers that identify the ownership of the model. Although backdoor-based watermarks can be verified through black-box access, they are usually zero-bit, meaning the watermark can only demonstrate its presence or absence instead of a bit string representing identity.

Some recent works also explore applying DNN watermarks to FL copyright protection. WAFFLE [20] is the first watermarking scheme designed for FL, in which the Server is responsible for embedding backdoor-based watermarks into the FL model, using a retraining step after federated aggregation. Liu et al. [21,22] and Li et al. [23] propose to let the Clients embed both parameter-based and backdoor-based watermarks into the global model. However, existing works only focus on ownership verification, and none of them provides traceability of the model leakers for FL models. Even if the FL group can prove ownership of the FL model in the event of infringement, it is not capable of detecting the model leakers hidden among them.

We aim to design an FL copyright protection framework that furnishes both ownership verification and traceability for the FL model. In this paper, we present FedTracker, the first FL model protection framework that offers both. The problem and our framework are illustrated in Fig. 1. Specifically, we design a bi-level protection scheme that enables ownership verification and traceability respectively. On one level, FedTracker embeds a global watermark into the aggregated global model in each iteration, so that when copyright infringement occurs the FL group can extract the watermark and verify ownership. On the other level, before distributing the model in each iteration, the server inserts a unique local fingerprint for each Client to identify each model. The model leaker can then be traced by disclosing the identification inside the model.

However, there are two main challenges in implementing such a framework:

- It is challenging to preserve the utility of the model when natural data is lacking. Since the server is assumed to have no access to the training data, it needs to embed a watermark trigger set that is out of the distribution of natural data, which may significantly compromise the model's utility.

- It is challenging to guarantee the discrimination of different models. Since we need to embed and compare multiple different fingerprints from different Clients, there is a higher requirement on the identifiability and robustness of the Clients' fingerprints.

To tackle these challenges, we first propose a watermark embedding algorithm based on Continual Learning (CL) [24] to improve the utility of the watermarked model. We regard the primitive task of FL and the watermark embedding task as learning data from different domains, so the utility drop can be attributed to catastrophic forgetting [24] while learning a different task. Inspired by the Gradient Episodic Memory (GEM) [25], we design a CL-based embedding algorithm for the FL scenario, so that utility is better preserved during watermark embedding. We introduce this algorithm in Section IV-B.

Second, to enhance the differentiation between the models of different Clients, we generate fingerprints by minimizing the maximal distance between fingerprints. We also propose a Fingerprint Similarity Score (FSS) to measure the similarity of the extracted fingerprint and the Clients' fingerprints. Compared with traditional hamming distance, whose output is discrete, FSS provides a more fine-grained measurement because its output is continuous, and thus better discriminates different fingerprints. Moreover, we embed the watermark and the fingerprints into different parts of the model to lower their mutual impact and improve the effectiveness of both mechanisms. The details are presented in Section IV-C.

## I-A Contributions

Our main contributions can be summarized as follows:

- We propose the first FL ownership verification and traceability framework, FedTracker. Its bi-level protection scheme, consisting of the global watermark mechanism and the local fingerprint mechanism, provides ownership verification and traceability respectively. Experimental results show that FedTracker also provides tremendous fidelity and robustness against various attacks.

- Inspired by Continual Learning (CL), we design a CL-based watermark embedding algorithm for the FL scenario, which maintains the utility of the FL model on both the primitive task and the watermark task while embedding the watermark.

- We propose an optimization-based fingerprint generation method and a novel metric named Fingerprint Similarity Score (FSS). Together they help distinguish different fingerprints and improve the effectiveness of tracing the culprit.

## I-B Roadmap

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section II introduces the background knowledge of FedTracker. Section III formulates the copyright protection problem in FL, including the definitions of ownership verification and traceability and the threat model. Section IV presents the procedure of FedTracker and the solutions to the key challenges above. Section V gives a detailed implementation description of FedTracker. Section VI presents the experiments evaluating FedTracker's performance, and Section VII concludes this paper.
